the overall efficiency is not the most suitable parameter based on the 1st law of thermodynamics to quantify the fuel savings in combined refrigeration and electricity generation systems.
the primary energy rate is the most well-suitted parameter of performance based upon the first law to quantify the performance of a combined refrigeration and Power (CPR) plant.

a parameter of performance based only on the first law should be used to compare the performance of CRP plants, the overall efficiency is not a parameter based on a single law of thermodynamics, and the primary energy rate is a parameter of performance that is mathematically consistent with the first law.

the overall efficiency is not a parameter based on first law and, therefore, should not be used to quantify the performance of CRP plants, since it does not represent any physical quantity.
the primary energy rate is the best parameter based on the First Law to quantify the fuel economy of a CRP system.

, in a CRP plant, it is more convenient to define the overall efficiency as the ratio between the total useful energy produced by the plant (electric and thermal) and the primary fuel energy consumed by the plant, and not as the ratio between electric and thermal energy produced by the CRP plant and the primary fuel consumption.

the overall efficiency is not a well-defined parameter of performance based only on the first law.
the primary energy rate is the parameter of performance that best represents the overall performance of a CR.
